title: Impact of Merit Scholarships on College Enrollment

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

The most appropriate causal method for this research question is a **Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)**.

**Why RDD?**
The research scenario explicitly describes a situation where treatment (merit scholarship) is assigned based on whether a student meets a specific GPA threshold (a "cutoff" in the running variable). Students just above the cutoff receive the scholarship, while those just below do not. This sharp cutoff rule, applied to a continuous running variable (GPA), is the hallmark of a sharp RDD. By comparing students infinitesimally close to the GPA cutoff, we can isolate the causal effect of the scholarship, as these students are expected to be very similar in all unobservable characteristics relevant to college enrollment, differing primarily only by their scholarship eligibility.

**Key Assumption

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: The analysis exploits the GPA threshold as a cutoff to compare students just above and below the threshold.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Meeting the GPA threshold for a merit scholarship significantly increases college enrollment rates.
